question: Does a soliton crystal (the archived lab's lattice, untrained, pushed by a constant torque) hold a world's rhythm, and is that hold collective: tighter with size and coupling, more robust to noise?
seeds: seed(name) = int(sha256('<registration id>:<beacon randomness>:<name>').hexdigest()[:12], 16) for each cell name (the noise of its trajectories) and for 'crystal' (the gyroscope W); numpy PCG64.
beacon: drand quicknet (chain 52db9ba70e0cc0f6eaf7803dd07447a1f5477735fd3f661792ba94600c84e971): the first round dated at or after the earliest GitHub-witnessed push (GET repos/s0fractal/time-lab/activity) that holds the commit adding q2-crystal/registration.lock.json.

design.loose: kappa = 0 and g_lat = 0: the same pinned oscillators, uncoupled

hypotheses.statement: A larger soliton crystal locks to a world's rhythm more tightly: at σ = 0.3 its lock gain at least doubles from N = 2 to N = 8 and again from N = 8 to N = 32.
hypotheses.rule: G = D without the rhythm (F1 = 0) / D with it (F1 = 0.6) for one (coupling, N, σ, j); D = var(ΔJ) / (2 Δt N d) over the window [150, 600] of 1024 trajectories. Each test is log10 of a ratio of two gains, with a 95% percentile interval over 2000 resamples of every cell's trajectories, seeded from the registration id; inconclusive whenever a gain is undefined. Supported if both intervals (G(8)/G(2), G(32)/G(8)) lie above log10 2; contradicted if either lies wholly below log10 2; else inconclusive.

hypotheses.statement: The lock is collective: at N = 32 and σ = 0.3 the coupled crystal's lock gain is at least ten times that of the same pinned oscillators uncoupled (κ = g_lat = 0).
hypotheses.rule: G = D without the rhythm (F1 = 0) / D with it (F1 = 0.6) for one (coupling, N, σ, j); D = var(ΔJ) / (2 Δt N d) over the window [150, 600] of 1024 trajectories. Each test is log10 of a ratio of two gains, with a 95% percentile interval over 2000 resamples of every cell's trajectories, seeded from the registration id; inconclusive whenever a gain is undefined. Supported if the interval of G(crystal)/G(loose) lies above 1 (log10 10); contradicted if it lies wholly below 1; else inconclusive.

hypotheses.statement: Size buys robustness to noise: at σ = 0.5 the lock gain of the N = 32 crystal is at least five times that of the N = 8 crystal.
hypotheses.rule: G = D without the rhythm (F1 = 0) / D with it (F1 = 0.6) for one (coupling, N, σ, j); D = var(ΔJ) / (2 Δt N d) over the window [150, 600] of 1024 trajectories. Each test is log10 of a ratio of two gains, with a 95% percentile interval over 2000 resamples of every cell's trajectories, seeded from the registration id; inconclusive whenever a gain is undefined. Supported if the interval of G(32)/G(8) at σ = 0.5 lies above log10 5; contradicted if it lies wholly below log10 5; else inconclusive.

hypotheses.statement: The archived lab's gyroscope (j_scale 0.1, J = j_scale (W − Wᵀ)) weakens the lock: at N = 32 and σ = 0.3 it lowers the crystal's lock gain at least twofold. Not calibrated: a prediction made blind.
hypotheses.rule: G = D without the rhythm (F1 = 0) / D with it (F1 = 0.6) for one (coupling, N, σ, j); D = var(ΔJ) / (2 Δt N d) over the window [150, 600] of 1024 trajectories. Each test is log10 of a ratio of two gains, with a 95% percentile interval over 2000 resamples of every cell's trajectories, seeded from the registration id; inconclusive whenever a gain is undefined. Supported if the interval of G(j = 0.1)/G(j = 0) lies below −log10 2; contradicted if it lies wholly above −log10 2; else inconclusive.
